Build the grid and spline basis for the distribution of effects

Source: R/grid.R
make_efron_grid.Rd

The model represents the distribution of true effects, \(g\), by its probabilities on a grid of equally spaced points. The logarithm of these probabilities is, up to a normalizing constant, a linear combination of natural cubic spline functions (see bayes_efron_fit()). make_efron_grid() builds the grid and the spline basis from the estimates. bayes_efron_fit() builds its grid in the same way from its own arguments, so you only need to call this function yourself to inspect a grid before fitting, or to use one grid in several fits by passing it as grid.

Usage

make_efron_grid(
  theta_hat,
  sigma = NULL,
  ...,
  L = NULL,
  expansion = 0.5,
  M = 6L,
  grid_method = "pilot",
  theta_true = NULL,
  bound_expansion = NULL,
  support = NULL,
  component = c("point", "normal"),
  width = 2/3,
  knots = "grid",
  margin = 0.1,
  seed = NULL
)

# S3 method for class 'bef_grid'
format(x, digits = 3L, ...)

# S3 method for class 'bef_grid'
print(x, ...)

Arguments

theta_hat

Numeric vector of effect estimates, one per site. Can also be a data frame or a bef_data object that contains the estimates and their standard errors (see as_bef_data()), in which case sigma is omitted.

sigma

Numeric vector of standard errors of the estimates. All must be positive.

...

For make_efron_grid(), these dots are for future extensions and must be empty; the arguments after them must be named. The print() method passes them on to format().

L

Number of grid points, an integer from 51 to 401. If NULL (the default), the number is chosen from the data: 101, or more if 101 points are too few for the standard errors or for the spread of the effects. See Details.

expansion

Expansion factor, a number between 0 and 5. With grid_method = "pilot" or "paper_realdata", the range of theta_hat is extended on each side by expansion times its width.

M

Number of spline functions, an integer from 3 to 10. More spline functions allow \(g\) to have narrower features. In simulated data sets of 1,500 sites, the site intervals contained somewhat fewer of the true effects with 8 functions than with 6 (see vignette("twin-towers")).

grid_method

Method for choosing the limits of the grid: "pilot" (the default), "paper_realdata", "paper_simulation" or "paper_sensitivity". See Details. "pilot" requires CmdStan; the others do not.

theta_true

Numeric vector of true effects, the same length as theta_hat. Required by "paper_simulation" and "paper_sensitivity", which are intended for simulations.

bound_expansion

Expansion factor for grid_method = "paper_sensitivity", a number greater than 0 and at most 5: the range of theta_true is extended on each side by bound_expansion times its width. NULL (the default) is equivalent to 0.5.

support

Numeric vector of length 2 with the lower and upper limits of the grid. If NULL (the default), the limits are chosen by grid_method.

component

Type of component at each grid point: "point" (the default) for a point mass, or "normal" for a normal distribution.

width

Standard deviation of the normal components in units of the grid spacing, a number greater than 0 and at most 2. Only used with component = "normal".

knots

Method for placing the knots of the spline functions. Currently only "grid" is available; see Details.

margin

Margin for grid_method = "pilot", a number between 0 and 1. The interval that contains the central 99.9% of the pilot estimate of \(g\) is extended on each side by margin times its width.

seed

Integer seed for the pilot fit, only used with grid_method = "pilot". If NULL (the default), a seed is taken from the clock.

x

A bef_grid object created by make_efron_grid().

digits

Number of significant digits to print.

Value

An object of class bef_grid, which is a list with the following components.

grid

The grid points.

B

The spline basis, a matrix with one row per grid point and M columns.

L, M

The number of grid points and the number of spline functions.

support

The lower and upper limits of the grid.

spacing

The distance between neighboring grid points.

grid_method

The method that chose the limits, or "support" if they were specified directly.

expansion

The factor by which the range was extended (NA if the method does not use one).

component

"point" or "normal".

width

The value of width (NA for point masses).

tau_c

The standard deviation of a component (0 for point masses).

knots

A list with the method and the positions of the interior and boundary knots.

resolution

A list that compares the grid spacing with the data, as described in Details. It contains the two ratios, sigma_min_over_spacing and scale_over_spacing; L_needed, the smallest number of points for which both are large enough; adequate, which is TRUE if they are large enough for this grid; L_chosen, which is TRUE if the number of points was chosen from the data; share_outside_estimates, the proportion of grid points outside the range of the estimates; and width_over_sigma, the width of the grid divided by the median standard error.

attribution

A list with the formula of the method (formula) and its source (source).

pilot

Only for grid_method = "pilot": a list that records what the method did. wide is the initial range and core is the interval that contained the central 99.9% of the pilot estimate of \(g\). narrowed is TRUE if the range was narrowed, share is the proportion of the initial range that remains, and protected contains the sites whose estimates caused a limit to be moved outward. margin and seed are the values that were used. chains, iter_warmup and iter_sampling give the length of the pilot fit (zero if none was run), diagnostics contains its sampler diagnostics, and seconds is its run time.

data

A list with the estimates and standard errors from which the grid was built, used by plot.bef_grid(). It is not included in the grid stored in a fit.

Details

The grid is determined by four choices.

  • The range, which is either chosen by the method named in grid_method or specified directly as support.

  • The number of grid points, L.

  • What \(g\) places at each grid point, component. With "point" (the default, and the model of Lee and Sui, 2025) it is a point mass. With "normal" it is a normal distribution whose standard deviation is width times the grid spacing, as in the penalized Gaussian mixture of Sui and Tipton (2026).

  • The flexibility of \(g\), which depends on the number of spline functions, M, and on the placement of their knots, knots.

There are four methods for choosing the range. Three of them come from the code that accompanies Lee and Sui (2025), and "pilot" narrows the range of the first of them.

grid_methodLimits of the gridNeeds theta_true
"paper_realdata"The range of theta_hat, extended on each side by expansion times its width.No
"pilot"The range of "paper_realdata", narrowed to the region where a short preliminary fit on that range (the pilot fit) places \(g\).No
"paper_simulation"The range of theta_true, extended by 0.5 (in the units of the effects) on each side.Yes
"paper_sensitivity"The range of theta_true, extended on each side by bound_expansion times its width.Yes

Use "pilot" (the default) or "paper_realdata" for real data; "paper_realdata" does not require a model fit. The other two methods need the true effects, so they can only be used in simulations. They are provided so that the paper's simulations can be reproduced.

With the default expansion, the range of "paper_realdata" is twice as wide as the range of the estimates, and the estimates are themselves more spread out than the true effects. With many sites, \(g\) then occupies only a small part of the grid, most of the spline functions describe the empty part, and sampling is inefficient. The "pilot" method avoids this in two steps.

  1. A pilot fit is run on the range of "paper_realdata", with 4 chains of 500 warmup and 500 sampling iterations, 101 grid points and 6 spline functions. The pilot fit always uses point masses, even when the final grid has normal components.

  2. The method finds the grid points that enclose the central 99.9% of the pilot estimate of \(g\) and extends this interval on each side by margin times its width, and by at least one grid spacing of the pilot fit. If an estimate lies more than 4 of its standard errors outside a limit, the limit is moved out to that estimate plus or minus 2 standard errors.

The limits never go beyond the range of "paper_realdata", so the method either narrows that range or leaves it unchanged. It leaves the range unchanged for raudenbush1985 and krw_discrimination and narrows it for twin_towers; see vignette("choosing-a-grid"). If the range of "paper_realdata" is narrower than the median standard error, no pilot fit is run. The method requires CmdStan. Specify seed to make the result reproducible. The pilot component of the result records what the method did.

If support = c(lower, upper) is specified, the grid runs from lower to upper and no method is applied, so grid_method must not be specified. With point masses, \(g\) has no probability outside the support, so the support is the set of values that an effect can take in the model. With normal components, the support is the range of the component centers, and \(g\) extends about 2 component standard deviations further on each side. If the effects must stay within given bounds, use point masses together with reading = "step" in the summaries, because with the default reading a summary can extend half a grid spacing beyond a limit (see g_summary()).

With knots = "grid", the spline basis is splines::ns(grid, df = M, intercept = FALSE). The interior knots are at quantiles of the grid points, which makes them equally spaced over the grid, and the boundary knots are at its limits. An error is thrown if the basis together with a constant column does not have full column rank; a smaller M avoids this.

The grid must also be fine enough for the data. With point masses, the likelihood of a site is evaluated only at the grid points, so a site whose standard error is much smaller than the grid spacing is represented poorly. In addition, a grid with only a few points across the bulk of the effects cannot show the shape of \(g\). The function computes two ratios to check this.

  • The smallest standard error divided by the grid spacing, which should be at least 0.75.

  • A rough estimate of the standard deviation of the effects divided by the grid spacing, which should be at least 4. With \(m\) the median absolute deviation of the estimates (scaled as in stats::mad(), so that it estimates a standard deviation) and \(v\) the median sampling variance, this estimate is \(\sqrt{m^2 - v}\), or \(\sqrt{v}\) if \(m^2 - v\) is not positive.

With L = NULL, the grid has 101 points if both ratios are large enough, and otherwise the smallest number of points, up to 401, for which they are. With normal components only the second ratio is used, in an equivalent form: the standard deviation of a component should be at most one sixth of the estimated standard deviation of the effects. A standard error smaller than the grid spacing is not a problem in that case. A warning of class bef_warn_grid_resolution is issued if a ratio is too small for the returned grid, or if the whole grid is narrower than the median standard error. The warning message suggests what to change. The ratios are stored in the resolution component of the result.

Functions

  • format(bef_grid): Returns the lines that print() shows as a character vector.

  • print(bef_grid): Prints the limits and the spacing of the grid, the method that chose the limits, the components, the spline functions with their knots, and how the spacing compares with the data.

References

Lee, J. and Sui, D. (2025). Fully Bayesian inference for meta-analytic deconvolution using Efron's log-spline prior. Mathematics, 13(16), 2639. doi:10.3390/math13162639

Sui, D. and Tipton, E. (2026). Meta-analysis without normality: estimating the true effect distribution with penalized Gaussian mixtures. arXiv:2604.27887.

See also

bayes_efron_fit(), compare_efron_grids(), vignette("choosing-a-grid")

Examples

# The default method runs the pilot fit, which needs CmdStan.
if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
make_efron_grid(twin_towers$yi, twin_towers$sei, seed = 20250627)
} # }

# The method "paper_realdata" needs no fit.
grid <- make_efron_grid(krw_discrimination, grid_method = "paper_realdata")
grid
#> <bef_grid> 101 points from -0.0829 to 0.159, spacing 0.00241
#>   Rule:       "paper_realdata", expansion 0.5
#>   Component:  point masses
#>   Basis:      6 natural cubic spline functions, knots by rule "grid"
#>   Interior knots: -0.0427, -0.00242, 0.0378, 0.0781, 0.118
#>   Resolution: smallest standard error 2.21 spacings, scale of the effects 7.89 spacings
#>   50.5% of the grid points lie outside the range of the estimates
range(krw_discrimination$yi)
#> [1] -0.02254064  0.09817050
grid$support
#> [1] -0.08289621  0.15852607
dim(grid$B)
#> [1] 101   6

# The six spline functions and the knots over the estimates, in
# percentage points.
plot(grid, scale = 100)


# A wider grid with more spline functions.
wide <- make_efron_grid(krw_discrimination, grid_method = "paper_realdata",
                        expansion = 1, M = 8)
wide$support
#> [1] -0.1432518  0.2188816

# The limits specified directly, and a normal distribution at each grid
# point.
make_efron_grid(krw_discrimination, support = c(-0.05, 0.15),
                component = "normal")
#> <bef_grid> 101 points from -0.05 to 0.15, spacing 0.002
#>   Rule:       ends given in `support`
#>   Component:  normal, standard deviation 0.00133 (0.667 of the spacing)
#>   Basis:      6 natural cubic spline functions, knots by rule "grid"
#>   Interior knots: -0.0167, 0.0167, 0.05, 0.0833, 0.117
#>   Resolution: smallest standard error 2.67 spacings, scale of the effects 9.52 spacings
#>   39.6% of the grid points lie outside the range of the estimates

# In a simulation the true effects can set the range.
sim <- make_efron_grid(twin_towers, grid_method = "paper_simulation",
                       theta_true = twin_towers$theta_true)
sim$support
#> [1] -2.198691  3.197622
